item.subject: science
item.stem:
Komal asks why rocks, soil, and minerals of Earth's crust support life. Soil forms as rocks break down with remains of plants and animals and can hold nutrients such as nitrogen and potassium. Varied landforms create different habitats.

Which claim is correct?

options.A: Rocks break down with remains of plants and animals to form soil that holds nutrients life needs, and varied landforms create different habitats.
options.B: Nutrient-rich habitats form first, and that then causes rocks to break down into soil.
options.C: Rocks, soil, and minerals support life only when they are themselves living things.
options.D: Varied landforms matter for life only because they make Earth's surface look different.
